paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think Jesus is doing in this whole chapter. He keeps pulling our eyes off everybody else and turning them toward our own lives. He says, "First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother's eye." (Matthew 7:5) And He sums up how to treat people in one line: "In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you." (Matthew 7:12)

He also wants us to know who we're talking to. "Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you." (Matthew 7:7) If a dad who is evil knows how to give good gifts, then "how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him!" (Matthew 7:11) So the narrow gate isn't a trick. It's a road to life, and the Father is the one who welcomes you onto it. (Matthew 7:13-14)

Then Jesus lands the plane, and it's about doing, not just saying. "Not everyone who says to Me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only he who does the will of My Father in heaven." (Matthew 7:21) Everyone who hears His words and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock, and that house stood because "its foundation was on the rock." (Matthew 7:24-25) So, baker, listen to Jesus, then DO what He says, because that's the foundation you can stand on. This was the last part of the Sermon on the Mount, and the crowds were astonished, because He taught as one who had authority. (Matthew 7:28-29)
